newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two Buba officials see Germany making EMU grade.
newsitem.headline: Two Buba officials see Germany making EMU grade.

text.p: There are now no inflationary dangers on the horizon in Germany to threaten growth, leaving the country a chance to meet the entry criteria to Europe's planned currency union, a senior Bundesbank official said.
"There are no signs of renewed inflationary dangers," Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister told journalists at the sidelines of a banking congress.
Separately, Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher, also a Bundesbank council member said he believed Germany would meet the economic conditions for EMU entry.

"We will make it. I am convinced of that," he said in answer to a question. Meister said there were no dangers signs of wages picking up or consumer prices to suddenly pick up again and added "we can be satisfied" with current inflation levels.
But he added "we must be careful that the trend is not reversed."
In light of an expected pickup in economic growth, Meister also said the chances were there for Germany to meet the entry criteria for Europe's currency union.
"The chances (for Germany to make it) are there given expected tax revenues, consolidation plans and expected growth," Meister said.
